rows.text: Two great circles govern ecosystems: matter cycles while time marches. In the carbon cycle, photosynthesis and respiration trade CO₂ between air and life, with fossil fuels and limestone as deep sinks — until combustion and deforestation overload the balance.…

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Nitrification vs nitrogen fixation:** fixation = N₂ → NH₃ (Rhizobium, cyanobacteria); nitrification = NH₃ → NO₂⁻ → NO₃⁻ (Nitrosomonas, Nitrobacter).  ·  **Denitrification vs ammonification:** denitrification returns NO₃⁻ to N₂ gas (Pseudomonas); ammonification releases NH₃ from dead matter.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: NEB expects detailed, labelled diagrams of the carbon and nitrogen cycles.  ·  The role of bacteria (Rhizobium, Nitrosomonas, Pseudomonas) in the nitrogen cycle is a very common exam point.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Short answer (2m):** What is a climax community? **Answer.** The **stable, self-perpetuating final community** of ecological succession, in equilibrium with the regional climate. It has maximum biomass and biodiversity and changes little unless the climate or substrate itself changes (e.g. the mixed forest that ends a xerosere).

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Facilitation:** each seral stage modifies the environment so the next stage can establish — succession is ecosystem engineering by life itself.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Carbon cycle: photosynthesis ↔ respiration; fossil-fuel combustion and deforestation raise CO₂ → greenhouse effect; ocean and limestone are sinks.  ·  Nitrogen cycle: fixation (Rhizobium, Azotobacter, Anabaena, lightning, Haber) → nitrification (Nitrosomonas, Nitrobacter) → assimilation → ammonification → denitrification (Pseudomonas).  ·  Succession: directional change → climax. Primary (xerosere: lichen → moss → herb → shrub → forest) vs secondary (faster, soil present). Sere, seral stages, pioneer, climax.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: The Haber process now fixes more nitrogen than all natural terrestrial sources combined — humanity's biggest intervention in a biogeochemical cycle.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: L = NΦ/I  ·  Carbon cycle: CO2 ↔ organic C (photosynthesis/respiration/decomposition); fossil fuel combustion → CO2  ·  Nitrogen cycle: N2 → (fixation) NH3 → (nitrification) NO2- → NO3- → (assimilation) plants → (ammonification) NH3 → (denitrification) N2

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Succession: primary (bare rock) / secondary (existing soil) → climax community  ·  **Primary vs secondary succession:** primary starts lifeless (no soil); secondary restarts after disturbance with soil intact.  ·  Primary vs secondary succession: key difference is the starting point (bare rock vs existing soil).
